cands.name: Daphne Campbell
cands.bio: Registered nurse (BSN). Florida House District 108, 2010-2016; Florida Senate District 38, 2016-2018. Lost the 2018 Senate primary to Jason Pizzo. Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary for HD 108.
cands.local_ties: Born in Cap-Haitien, Haiti (1957). Haitian-American; represented northeast Miami-Dade for most of 2010-2018. Ran for North Miami mayor in 2024 per BallotReady. Current residence not stated in sources found.

record.text: Florida House, District 108, three terms 2010-2016; Florida Senate, District 38, 2016-2018 (Wikipedia).
Other races: Senate District 35 Democratic primary 2020 (placed second per Wikipedia); North Miami mayor 2024 general per BallotReady.
Campaign site says she secured $3.7M in local project funding, '$125M+' for District 38 and $25M for cancer research; these are the campaign's own claims, not independently verified.

controversies.text: In 2012 the Miami Herald asked Campbell about $145,000 in IRS liens against her. She replied "I don't have no tax liens," though the paper had federal documents showing otherwise. The state Democratic Party then asked her to resign. Former business partners also accused the Campbells of scamming them, and she denied wrongdoing.

In a June 2020 Sun-Sentinel candidate questionnaire, Campbell answered "Never" when asked if she had been a party to a civil lawsuit, including foreclosure. Florida Politics found court records naming her in 10 cases, nine as defendant, including at least seven foreclosures.

In 2006 the state ended its contract with Professional Group Homes, the company Campbell ran with her husband, closing all ten group homes. Four residents died within a year, and inspectors found rodent droppings and dead roaches. Campbell denied wrongdoing and declined to discuss the deaths (Miami New Times, 2010).

In 2018, while running for state Senate, Campbell's campaign sent a flyer claiming Aventura Commissioner Robert Shelley's endorsement, though he backed her opponent. After Florida Politics reported it, her campaign apologized in a letter to Shelley and blamed a staff mix-up. Shelley accepted the apology.
